title-group.article-title: Tocilizumab for Steroid Pulse-Refractory Cytokine Release Syndrome in Chemotherapy With Durvalumab Plus Tremelimumab for NSCLC: A Case Report

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.p: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have dramatically improved the prognosis of NSCLC. However, various immune-related adverse events (irAEs) have been reported. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is an irAE that is occasionally severe and life-threatening. CRS is a major irAE of the chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy and a rare irAE for anti–programmed cell death protein-1 and programmed death-ligand 1 therapy. Therefore, reports of CRS were rare in NSCLC, but after approval of anti–programmed cell death protein-1 and anti–programmed death-ligand 1 plus anti–CTLA-4 antibodies, reports of CRS are increasing. We, here, report two cases of successful tocilizumab treatment for steroid pulse–refractory CRS in chemotherapy with durvalumab plus tremelimumab for NSCLC.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Lung cancer is the most common cause of cancer death worldwide, but recent advances in immunotherapy using immune checkpoint inhibitors have dramatically improved the prognosis. However, various immune-related adverse events (irAEs) have been reported.1

Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is an irAE that is occasionally severe and life-threatening. CRS is a major irAE of the chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy and a rare irAE for anti–programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) and anti–programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) therapy.2 Therefore, reports of CRS were rare in NSCLC, but after approval of anti–PD-1 and PD-L1 plus anti–CTLA-4 antibodies, reports of CRS are increasing.3,4 Tocilizumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor and is approved for the treatment of CRS. One report revealed three fatal cases despite steroid pulse therapy (SPT), and tocilizumab was not used in these cases.3 Although tocilizumab is established as a guideline-recommended treatment against CRS in CAR-T therapy, there are few reports suggesting the clinical effectiveness of tocilizumab for solid tumors, including NSCLC. We, here, report two cases of successful tocilizumab treatment for steroid pulse–refractory CRS in chemotherapy with durvalumab plus tremelimumab (D+T) for NSCLC.

sec.title: Case 1
sec.p: A 57-year-old man with stage IVA lung adenocarcinoma received four cycles of chemotherapy (carboplatin plus nab-paclitaxel) with D+T. He had a T3 (>5 cm) primary lung mass, right hilar and mediastinal lymph node metastases, and bilateral multiple lung metastases, representing a relatively high baseline tumor burden (Fig. 1A). Fifteen days after the last dose of D+T, he developed a fever of 40°C, rash (grade 1), and pneumonia (grade 3), resulting in hospitalization (Fig. 1B). Antibiotics and SPT (methylprednisolone, 1g/day for 3 days) were initiated. Nevertheless, the symptoms and pneumonia did not improve (Fig. 1C), circulating levels of IL-6 were elevated at 171 pg/mL, and blood and urine cultures were negative. There was no splenomegaly, hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction, markedly elevated ferritin levels, and pancytopenia. On the basis of these findings, sepsis, tumor lysis syndrome, and macrophage activation syndrome were unlikely, leading to a diagnosis of CRS, and tocilizumab was administered. Symptoms of fever and pneumonia recovered immediately (Figs. 1D and 2A). The primary lesion of the lung was found to have regrowth at the time CRS occurred, and he was moved to the next treatment (docetaxel plus ramucirumab) after CRS recovery.

sec.title: Case 2
sec.p: A 52-year-old man with postoperative recurrence of lung adenocarcinoma had a mediastinal lymph node metastasis and a right rib metastasis, representing a relatively low baseline tumor burden. He developed a fever of 40°C, rash (grade 3), and mucositis oral (grade 3) on day 10 after the first administration of chemotherapy (carboplatin plus pemetrexed) with D+T (Fig. 3). SPT and antibiotics were attempted, but the fever did not recede, and hypotension was also noted with IL-6 elevation to 756 pg/mL. Blood and urine cultures were negative. There was no splenomegaly, hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction, markedly elevated ferritin levels, and pancytopenia. Therefore, he was diagnosed with CRS rather than sepsis, tumor lysis syndrome, or macrophage activation syndrome, and given tocilizumab. Fever and hypotension improved promptly, and rash and mucositis oral disappeared gradually (Fig. 2B). Stable disease was obtained for 3 months after CRS recovery. Local progression was then confirmed, and we performed local ablative radiotherapy.

caption.p: Image of skin rash at the onset of cytokine release syndrome in case 2. Redness and bulging rash on the face and back were observed, and oral mucositis.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: CRS is a systemic reaction caused by certain drugs. Symptoms include flulike fever, fatigue, rash, arthralgia, and myalgia in mild cases, or high fever, hypotension, and hypoxemia in severe cases.5 The National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines recommend the use of tocilizumab before steroids for the treatment of CRS associated with CAR-T therapy. On the other hand, steroids may be preceded by CRS induced by anti–PD-1 and PD-L1 plus anti–CTLA-4 antibodies, because it is difficult to distinguish it from other irAEs. In our cases, SPT was initiated with the concern of possible CRS, we were, thus, able to administer tocilizumab soon after the judgment of steroid pulse failure.

One factor that may predict the occurrence and severity of CRS is the disease burden. One report indicated that baseline overall tumor burden was a risk factor for developing severe irAEs in patients treated with anti–PD-1 and PD-L1 plus anti–CTLA-4 antibodies.6 In our cases, case 1 had a relatively high baseline tumor burden, whereas case 2 did not. Some CRS cases have a relationship between tumor burden and the severity of CRS, whereas other cases suffer from severe CRS that are associated with other factors but not with tumor burdens.

To our knowledge, this is the first report of tocilizumab for steroid pulse-refractory CRS in chemotherapy with D+T for NSCLC. The clinical spread of chemotherapy with D+T will require early recognition of severe CRS and proper tocilizumab use.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: We experienced two cases of tocilizumab for steroid pulse-refractory CRS in chemotherapy with D+T for NSCLC. Oncologists should consider tocilizumab in steroid pulse–refractory CRS cases during anti–PD-1 and PD-L1 plus anti–CTLA-4 antibodies therapy for NSCLC.
